classified.text: The user shall be able to create a new account by providing required personal information and receive a signed JWT upon successful registration.
Bank of Anthos shall validate user credentials during login and issue a time‑limited access token for authenticated sessions.
The system shall verify the integrity and expiration of JWTs on every request to protected resources.
Account holders shall be able to retrieve the current balance of each of their accounts in real time.
Users can request a paginated transaction history filtered by date range, transaction type, or amount.
The user shall be able to add, edit, or delete payment contacts that can be selected as transfer recipients.
Account holders shall initiate fund transfers to their own accounts or to saved contacts, specifying amount and optional memo.
The system shall validate each transfer for sufficient available balance, compliance rules, and daily limits before execution.
Bank of Anthos shall record every successful transfer, deposit, or withdrawal in an immutable, durable ledger service.
The user shall be able to submit a deposit request, which the system shall acknowledge and reflect in the balance cache after ledger confirmation.
An administrator shall have read‑only access to audit logs of all ledger entries for compliance review.
The system shall update the balance cache atomically after each ledger‑committed transaction.
Users can receive email or SMS notifications summarizing the details of completed transactions.
The user shall be able to cancel a pending outbound transfer within a configurable 5‑minute window.
Bank of Anthos shall enforce rate limiting on login attempts to mitigate credential‑stuffing attacks.
An administrator shall configure retention periods and archival policies for ledger data.
The system shall support optional multi‑factor authentication during login for accounts that enable it.
Users shall be able to export their transaction history in CSV or PDF format for personal record‑keeping.
The platform shall achieve 99.95% availability across all microservices, measured on a monthly basis.
System shall automatically scale horizontally in response to CPU or request latency thresholds defined per service.
All inter‑service communication shall be encrypted with TLS 1.3 and mutual authentication where appropriate.
The application shall log audit‑relevant events to a centralized observability stack with a retention of at least 90 days.
Balance queries shall return results within 200 ms for 95% of requests under normal load.
The ledger service shall provide durability guarantees of at least three geographically separated replicas.
Deployment pipelines shall support zero‑downtime rolling updates for each independently deployable microservice.
The system shall enforce role‑based access control (RBAC) such that only authorized personnel can perform administrative functions.
All JWTs shall be signed using RSA‑256 keys rotated every 30 days, and private keys shall be stored in a hardware security module (HSM).
